question.:question/problem: Find the exact solution of the equation $9^{x-1}=30.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we take $\log_{9}$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}9^{x-1}&=30\\\log_{9}(9^{x-1})&=\log_{9}(30)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\log_b(b^c)=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x-1=\log_{9}(30).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-1&=\log_{9}(30)\\x&=\log_{9}(30)+1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=\log_{9}(30)+1$.

We take $\log_{7}$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}7^{x}&=12\\\log_{7}(7^{x})&=\log_{7}(12)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\log_b(b^c)=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x=\log_{7}(12).
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=\log_{7}(12)$.

$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we take $\log_{4}$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4^{x-4}&=26\\\log_{4}(4^{x-4})&=\log_{4}(26)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\log_b(b^c)=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x-4=\log_{4}(26).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-4&=\log_{4}(26)\\x&=\log_{4}(26)+4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=\log_{4}(26)+4$.

$$

First, we take $\log_{2}$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2^{x+2}&=36\\\log_{2}(2^{x+2})&=\log_{2}(36)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\log_b(b^c)=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x+2=\log_{2}(36).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2&=\log_{2}(36)\\x&=\log_{2}(36)-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=\log_{2}(36)-2$.

$$
